methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs a rigorous two-phase design: a large retrospective multicenter evaluation of 115,973 mammograms across five UK NHS screening services (three distinct workflows, multiple vendors) followed by prospective observational deployment at 12 sites (9,266 cases), with prespecified protocols, ethics approvals and ISRCTN registration (60839016, 88754382). A 39-month ground truth including interval and next-round cancers is used, sample size was powered per site (~25,000 women targeting >=80% power), and exclusion and replacement rules are explicitly defined with contamination prevention for women previously used for AI training/tuning. Statistical approach is exemplary: prespecified 5% noninferiority margin, one-sided tests at 0.025 with Holm-Bonferroni correction, Wald tests with Obuchowski variance for clustered paired binary data, McNemar extension for superiority, and 10,000-iteration bootstrapping for breast- and lesion-level CIs. Limitations (subgroup sample sizes, lack of interventional design, ground-truth exclusions) are explicitly acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The manuscript has direct, near-term clinical relevance: it evaluates a deployable AI system against real UK NHS Breast Screening Programme workflows, quantifies operational impact (32.1% reduction in reader time, 17.7-20.2% CDR increase, 25% detection of future interval cancers and 25.1% of next-round cancers), and exposes concrete implementation barriers (threshold drift, NBSS write-back limitations, paper-driven workflows). Findings directly inform UK national screening policy, guideline updates, and AI deployment frameworks, with fairness analyses across ethnicity, IMD, age and density. The design is a large multicenter cohort/diagnostic accuracy study with a prospective feasibility component and is not randomized or interventional, placing it at Oxford CEBM 2b (individual cohort study) rather than 1b.

reporting_quality.justification: As a diagnostic accuracy study, STARD is the most applicable standard; the paper reports index test (AI v1.2), reference standard (39-month follow-up including intervals and next-round cancers), inclusion/exclusion criteria, flow diagrams (Extended Data Fig. 1), subgroup and lesion-level analyses, and prespecified endpoints, meeting most STARD items. A Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced and protocols are attached as Supplementary Information, and ISRCTN registrations are provided. Gaps include no explicit STARD checklist, and data/code availability is limited: source data files are cited for figures/tables but raw mammography data are constrained by NHS governance and there is no explicit code repository or container, warranting a moderate data availability score.

novelty_literature.justification: The work extends McKinney et al. 2020 (ref 9) with an updated model (v1.2) and contributes several novel elements: systematic multi-workflow, multi-vendor UK NHS evaluation with 39-month ground truth including interval and next-round cancers, explicit fairness auditing across IMD/ethnicity/density/age, iterative adaptive OP calibration with observed distribution shift between tuning (2016) and deployment (2023), and breast- and lesion-level FROC analysis proposed as standard metrics. It is not first-in-class (MASAI, Lauritzen, Dembrower already demonstrated AI noninferiority) but meaningfully fills documented implementation and fairness gaps and contributes prospective feasibility insights rarely published. Novelty is solid extension rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is exceptionally well organized with clear structure across Main, Methods, Results and Discussion; subsection headings communicate findings directly (e.g., 'AI outperformed for first screens'). Tables 1-2 summarize service-level characteristics compactly, Figures 2-4 present multi-level performance (case/breast/lesion), ROC curves, subgroup breakdowns and weekly drift plots effectively, and Extended Data figures are cross-referenced throughout. Quantitative claims are consistently paired with 95% CIs and p-values, and limitations are discussed with appropriate nuance. Prose is precise, accessible to both clinical and technical readers, and publication-ready.

key_strengths: Large, multicenter UK NHS evaluation (115,973 retrospective + 9,266 prospective cases across 5 services and 12 sites with 3 vendors and 3 workflows)

Rigorous 39-month ground truth incorporating interval and next-round cancers, with prespecified 5% noninferiority margin and Holm-Bonferroni-corrected one-sided tests using Obuchowski variance and McNemar extensions
Clinically meaningful results: superior sensitivity (0.541 vs 0.437, P<0.001), noninferior specificity, 25.0% of interval cancers detected, 32.1% reader-time reduction with 17.7% CDR increase
Explicit fairness auditing across ethnicity, IMD, age, density and device with calibration analyses and transparent subgroup limitations

Prospective deployment surfaced and documented a real-world distribution shift between 2016 tuning and 2023 deployment, demonstrating iterative OP recalibration and informing regulatory change-control frameworks
Strong policy- and workflow-level implementation analysis (NBSS gaps, paper-driven workflows, arbitration burden modeling)
key_concerns: Observational rather than interventional design means downstream assessment-clinic costs, patient outcomes and human-AI interaction effects are not directly measured (deferred to companion study ref 14)

Some subgroup sample sizes (e.g., mixed ethnicity n=21 positives, IMD decile 1) remain underpowered, producing borderline noninferiority failures that the authors appropriately caveat but cannot fully resolve
Data availability is constrained by NHS governance and no explicit public code repository or container is described, limiting independent replication
Exclusion of women lacking follow-up negative screen may have removed underserved groups, acknowledged but unresolved
Prospective phase is short (8 weeks), limiting conclusions about long-term stability and drift detection in low-prevalence populations
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically rigorous, large-scale, multi-vendor NHS evaluation with prespecified endpoints and a genuine prospective deployment exposing real-world drift; clinical significance for national screening policy combined with fairness auditing places this at the top tier (Nature Medicine/Nature Cancer/Lancet Oncology scope), with only minor reporting refinements (explicit STARD checklist, code availability) warranted.
